Blackjack Rules

How to Play

Objective

Beat the dealer’s hand without going over 21

Betting

Each player will place their bets first, then receive two face up cards, while the dealer will receive two cards, one face up and the other face down

Player’s Turn

If the player didn’t hit Blackjack, they can choose to Hit, Double, Split, Stand, or Surrender

Dealer's Turn

When all players have finished their turns and at least one player hasn’t hit Blackjack or busted, the dealer reveals the face down card and continues drawing until the total equals 17 points or higher

Settlement

The settlement occurs when the dealer’s turn is finished (see Paytable)

Situational Rules

Insurance

If the dealer’s face up card is an Ace, players can place half of their bet as insurance; if the dealer hits Blackjack, the payout is 2:1; otherwise, the bet is won by the dealer

Double Down

Players can double their bets after the first two cards, receive one more card, and must then stand

Surrender

Before hitting, players can choose to surrender and reclaim half of their bets

Split

Players can divide a pair into two separate hands, requiring a bet equal to the original, and it can only be done once When splitting Aces, players receive only one additional card per hand, with no further hits allowed; If the player draws a 10-point card after splitting Aces, it is counted as 21 points, not as Blackjack
